summary: Tashi Tsering works in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the Central School for Tibetans and under many teachers, including Tenzin Gyatso. He was Research Officer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1979) and founded Amnye Machen Institute.

Tatiana Oranskaia specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1968–1974) and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (~1987–1988). She taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and served as professor at the University of Hamburg (1998–2016).

Tatsugen Sato is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from Komazawa University by 1978. He held teaching positions at Komazawa University (attested 1972–1978, 1994), Ryukoku University (attested 1974), and Tokai University.
Tatsuhiro Saito is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Tatsuo Hayashi worked in philosophy and history/archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University (~1919–1922), he held posts at Toyo University (~1925–1932), Tsuda University, Meiji University, Rikkyo University, and Hosei University.

Tatsuo Nishida was a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (1948–1956; doctorate 1962). He spent his career at Kyoto University (1956–1992) and later served at the National Center for Science Information Systems (1992–1994).

Tatsushi Tamai is a scholar in Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a Visiting Researcher at Soka University (attested 2013) and its International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (attested 2010–2016).

Tatyana Elizarenkova was an Indologist and linguist. She studied under Mikhaïl Peterson at Moscow State University's Philological Faculty (~1946–1951) and spent her career at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1957–2007).

Tavivat Puntarigvivat specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and under Luangpor Teean Jittasubho (1980). His posts include Kyoto University, Mahidol University (attested 2005), and the World Buddhist University (attested 2013).
Taw Sein Ko was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He pursued his education at the University of Rangoon, the Inner Temple (~1892–1893), and the Inns of Court (~1892–1893).

Teizo Iyanaga worked in history, archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1938), he held academic posts at Nagoya University (~1948–1956), the University of Tokyo (~1956–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).
Tej Ram Sharma is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctorate at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University around 1970.
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Lobsang Gyatso, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.

Tenga Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Benchen Monastery under Tai Situ Rinpoche, served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1967–1980), and founded Benchen Monastery in 1976.

Tensei Kitabatake was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1950–1955). He served as Ryukoku University's professor and president (1995–1999), and later as president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Sogen Omori and went on to found Chozen-ji.
Tenzin is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Philosophy degree at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik.

Tenzin Dorjee works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshes Lobsang Tsephel, Sonam Rinchen, and Dawa. He served as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and at Pullahari Monastery (attested 2000).

Tenzin Gyatso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers including Reting, Taktra, Ling, Trijang, Serkong, Khunu Lama, Trulshik, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoches, and founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists in 1989.
Tenzin L. Mullin is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at the University of Otago, supervised by Erica Baffelli and Elizabeth Guthrie.
